jobs.jobDescription:
Why Socure?

Socure is building the identity trust infrastructure for the digital economy — verifying 100% of good identities in real time and stopping fraud before it starts. The mission is big, the problems are complex, and the impact is felt by businesses, governments, and millions of people every day.

We hire people who want that level of responsibility. People who move fast, think critically, act like owners, and care deeply about solving customer problems with precision. If you want predictability or narrow scope, this won’t be your place. If you want to help build the future of identity with a team that holds a high bar for itself — keep reading.

Senior Technical Content Writer - Job Description

About the role

This is an employment marketing role for someone who can make exceptional engineers want to work at Socure. Socure is building AI-native infrastructure for identity, fraud prevention, and trust, and we need your help getting that engineering story out to the places where great technical talent discovers ideas, follows builders, and finds its next challenge.

You will work closely with engineers, technical leaders, recruiting, and marketing to turn APIs, machine learning models, identity graphs, and decisioning workflows into a compelling case for joining the team. Your work will show software engineers the problems they can solve here, the systems they can help build, and the ambition behind Socure's mission.

Why this role matters

The best engineers are not looking for generic employer branding. They are looking for hard technical problems, strong peers, meaningful architecture, and a mission worth their time. You will make those things visible - in the communities, publications, developer platforms, social channels, and other talent-rich spaces where engineers actually pay attention.

What you will do

Tell the engineering story

  • Interview engineers and technical leaders, learn how the platform works, and turn real technical work into stories that make top engineers lean in.

  • Write technical content - including engineering blogs, deep dives, architecture stories, technical whitepapers, and recruiting-facing website copy - that makes the work at Socure tangible.

Reach engineers where they are

  • Own an employment-marketing content calendar built around the channels and communities where software engineers discover work, exchange ideas, and decide which companies deserve their attention.

  • Adapt and distribute stories across developer platforms, technical publications, engineering communities, social channels, and other high-signal places where the best talent gathers.

  • Partner with recruiting and employer brand to connect content to talent goals, strengthen candidate interest, and support hard-to-fill engineering hiring.

Make difficult technology compelling

  • Translate APIs, machine learning models, identity graphs, decisioning workflows, and cloud-based architectures into accurate, engaging stories for technical audiences.

  • Show why the problems matter, what makes Socure's approach distinctive, and what an engineer could help build next.

Build real subject matter depth

  • Develop enough understanding of Socure's products and platform to write with authority, ask sharp questions, and earn the trust of technical experts.

  • Stay current on AI, fraud, identity, security, and infrastructure trends, and turn them into timely points of view that attract the right people.

How you will work

Collaborate across the company

  • Work with engineering, recruiting, employer brand, product marketing, and technical subject matter experts to find the strongest stories and get them ready for the right audiences.

  • Partner with design, social, and distribution teams to package and place content for reach, credibility, and candidate action.

  • Build a repeatable feedback loop with engineers so the content stays technically honest and genuinely representative of the work.

Raise the bar

  • Protect a high editorial standard for clarity, accuracy, voice, and consistency across every channel.

  • Edit and proofread content from other contributors, and help maintain Socure's content style guide.

Use AI thoughtfully

  • Use AI tools such as ChatGPT's Deep Research to accelerate research, drafting, and technical enablement while keeping human judgment, verification, and editorial quality at the center.

What you bring

  • Demonstrable experience in content writing, technical writing, employer brand, recruiting marketing, or content marketing, ideally in identity verification, fraud, cybersecurity, fintech, infrastructure, or another technical B2B SaaS environment.

  • Strong technical curiosity and the ability to learn and write accurately about APIs, machine learning, and cloud-based architectures.

  • Exceptional writing and storytelling skills, with a talent for making complex technical work clear, credible, and exciting to software engineers.

  • A portfolio of published technical, engineering, employer-brand, or recruiting content, such as blogs, deep dives, whitepapers, case studies, or similar work.

  • Experience partnering cross-functionally with engineering, recruiting, employer brand, product marketing, and subject matter experts.

  • Strong editorial and distribution instincts, with comfort owning a content calendar, finding the right audience and channel, giving and receiving feedback, and maintaining a consistent voice.

  • Experience using AI tools for research, drafting, and content production is a plus.

If you can understand ambitious engineering work, find the audience that will appreciate it, and make great engineers curious enough to start a conversation, we want to hear from you.

Socure is an equal opportunity employer that values diversity in all its forms within our company. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.
If you need an accommodation during any stage of the application or hiring process—including interview or onboarding support—please reach out to your Socure recruiting partner directly.

Follow Us!

YouTube | LinkedIn | X (Twitter) | Facebook

jobs.jobDescription:
CodePath is the largest educator of college computer science students in the country. We've trained over 50,000 students from more than 1,000 universities. Our partners include Amazon, Google, and other leading technology companies. After nearly a decade of training technical talent, we launched a $150M initiative with Anthropic to prepare people for careers in AI.

We're expanding into new markets and growing our team as AI changes the workforce. People joining CodePath now will help shape this next stage of our work.

We believe technical skills create opportunities. Our goal is to train millions of learners and create lasting economic impact. If you want to build something new, take ownership, and see the results of your work, this is a place to do it.

About the Role

Location: Remote (US)

Role Type: Full-Time Contractor (40 hours/week)

Duration: 9-month contract

Reports To: Sr. Manager, Development Operations

Compensation: $7,000–9,200 per month

This is not a traditional nonprofit grant writing role.

CodePath's Philanthropy Partnerships team raises the capital behind our courses, our career support, and our students' outcomes. The Grant Writer is how that case gets made. You write for national foundations and corporate partners deciding where their social impact dollars go, and you translate program data, student outcomes, and organizational strategy into the proposals and reports that win major commitments and steward them.

The second half of the job makes the first half repeatable. You partner with Finance, Delivery, Higher Education, and Data to stay ahead of fast-moving program updates and impact metrics, then turn what you learn into reusable assets, writing frameworks, and AI-enabled workflows the whole team draws on.

CodePath is an AI-native organization, and we expect this role to work like one. Writing faster with AI is table stakes. We want someone who builds the systems that raise everyone's output — so the team spends its time on strategy and judgment instead of rebuilding the same narrative from scratch.

CodePath is scaling fast. This is the role that lets our fundraising capacity scale with it.

Key Activities

Proposal development (~20%)

  • Lead or support major grant proposals, concepts, and letters of inquiry from prospecting through submission, meeting every funder guideline and submission requirement
  • Translate CodePath's mission, programs, and impact into compelling, consistent narratives the whole team can use
  • Research, synthesize, and translate program data into funder-facing briefs, proposals, and supporting materials
  • Build the frameworks and narratives that equip account owners to lead complex, high-value opportunities

Grant reporting and compliance (~10%)

  • Serve as lead or supporting writer on major funder reports
  • Equip account owners with the narratives, data, and frameworks they need to lead complex funder reports and steward high-value relationships
  • Proactively manage funder portal accounts, submission calendars, and organizational credentials
  • Keep internal grant management systems (e.g., Asana) current

Asset development and maintenance (~20%)

  • Build and maintain a shared library of reusable narrative assets — program descriptions, boilerplate language, proof points — that accelerates every proposal the team writes
  • Support fundraisers with ad-hoc narrative development

Cross-functional collaboration (~20%)

  • In partnership with the Sr. Manager of Development Operations, collaborate with other departments (e.g., Finance, Delivery, Higher Education, and Data) to collect and translate data, program updates, and student stories into funder-facing narratives
  • Supply narrative inputs, source content, program context, data, and proof points for donor-facing assets alongside fundraisers and the rest of the Philanthropy Partnerships team

Writing enablement and team optimization (~30%)

  • Use AI tools to improve how proposals, reports, and assets get built
  • Track fast-moving organizational developments and impact metrics to keep fundraising materials current and accurate
  • Develop and maintain proposal templates, writing frameworks, reusable assets, and funder-specific approaches that let account owners lead complex proposals and reports themselves
  • Document writing patterns and organizational knowledge to improve AI-assisted drafting and automate routine work, while holding quality, accuracy, and a consistent CodePath voice

Key Success Metrics

At 30 days

  • You understand CodePath's mission, program model, core narratives, impact data, and active funder portfolio
  • You know the team's proposal and reporting workflows, writing standards, and priorities
  • You have met the cross-functional teams and know where the information you need lives

At 60 days

  • You have contributed to active proposals or reports, turning existing CodePath information into clear, accurate funder-facing writing
  • You manage your assigned deliverables and deadlines, including funder requirements
  • You have added new or updated materials to the shared asset library
  • You have working relationships with key Finance, Delivery, Higher Education, and Data counterparts

At 90 days

  • You write proposals and reports that come back with strategic refinements, not substantive rewrites
  • You run assigned deliverables independently from information gathering through submission
  • You navigate cross-functional relationships efficiently to get what you need
  • The shared library is stronger — easier for the team to find, adapt, and keep current
  • You have shipped at least two repeatable or AI-enabled workflows that cut manual effort or free the team for higher-value work
  • Account owners are leading their own proposals and reports on complex opportunities, using frameworks and synthesis you built
  • You are a trusted writing partner to the Philanthropy Partnerships team

Qualifications

Required

  • 5–7 years writing for institutional and corporate funders — proposals, letters of inquiry, and funder reports. Long-form, funder-facing, and written by you.
  • You build with AI, you don't just write with it. You have documented recurring work, streamlined it with AI tools, and handed the result to other people. Using Claude or ChatGPT to polish a draft is not what we mean.
  • You do your own data synthesis. You go to the data and finance teams, ask the right questions, and turn what you get back into accurate narrative — without waiting for someone to hand you a summary.
  • You collaborate across functions and come in curious. You want to understand the programs and the strategy, not just the ask.
  • You work at pace. Concurrent deadlines, shifting priorities, and information that changes under you.
  • Exceptional writing and editing, with attention to detail while maintaining a strategic perspective.

Preferred

  • Experience in education, workforce development, or youth-serving nonprofits
  • Experience in a social impact, tech, or tech-adjacent environment
  • CRM management, HubSpot preferred
  • Asana or similar project management platforms
  • Comfort building simple visual assets (e.g., Canva)

Pay range

$7,000—$9,200 USD

100% Remote | Independent Contractor | 35 - 40 USD/hour

Help shape the future of AI.

Artificial Intelligence is evolving rapidly, and high-quality data plays a key role in making it smarter. We're looking for detail-oriented individuals to contribute to exciting AI projects by reviewing and annotating video content.

This is your opportunity to get involved in the world of AI, gain hands-on experience, and contribute to technologies shaping the future.

No previous AI or robotics experience required!

What you'll do

  • Review and annotate short video clips, identifying objects, actions, and events.
  • Evaluate video clarity, quality, and camera angles.
  • Assess movements and interactions based on project guidelines.
  • Ensure annotations are accurate and consistent.

What we're looking for

  • Excellent attention to detail and analytical thinking.
  • Good written English and ability to follow instructions.
  • Reliability and ability to work independently.
  • No previous AI, robotics, or annotation experience needed.


Why join?

  • Earn  35 - 40 USD/hour, depending on your country.
  • Work remotely from your location.
  • Gain hands-on experience supporting AI development.
  • Contribute to projects at the forefront of technology.


Get started

We currently have three projects open! Complete our certification process to demonstrate your skills and be considered for the opportunity that best matches your profile.

Your attention to detail could help shape what's next in AI!

This is an independent contractor opportunity. Project assignment and work availability are subject to certification results and project requirements.

jobs.jobDescription:
Summary of the Role

the Exploit (theexploit.co) is the security and tech industry's most trusted source of news that didn't happen. It's a satirical publication from Maze, an AI-native security company, covering the breaches, vendor launches, board meetings, AI news and compliance audits that are hilarious and totally made up, even when they don't feel like it.

We're hiring two satire content creators who can write a story and then turn it into a video. Each story runs as an article on the Exploit, then becomes a short social video, usually a 30- to 90-second news segment.

If you can shoot and edit the video yourself, that's a big plus. If you can't, your scripts need to be good enough that we'll happily make them for you. We'll take a great writer with no camera over a great camera with nothing to say.

Two formats we like: Matt Johansen's security news recaps, where one person covers one story fast with some comedy in it, and Ev Hand, who covers sports news in the article style we're after.

Some of our top articles, so you can see what works:

  1. French Locksmith Named Claude Launches Line of Padlocks; Cybersecurity Stocks Lose $18 Billion

  2. Judge Sentences CISO to 8 Consecutive Hours on RSA Expo Floor

  3. Meta Labs Proudly Announces Its AI Has Also Committed a Felony

  4. Burnt-Out CISO Forced to Decline Michelin-Starred Round Table Dinner

  5. Riot Breaks Out at Corporate Headquarters After Security Team Introduces Shift Left

Your Contributions to Our Journey

Writing

  • Pitch and write 400- to 700-word articles in the deadpan voice of a real newsroom covering an unreal industry

  • Pitch a lot of headlines and work them through with our team. The pieces are yours; we're there to keep the quality high.

Video

  • Write, and ideally shoot and edit, short news-desk videos

  • Turn our best articles into video, and pitch video-first stories of your own

Ideas

  • Test new formats, characters and recurring bits instead of repeating whatever worked last week

  • Bring material from your day job, with names changed to protect the guilty

What You Need to Be Successful

  • Real practitioner experience. You've worked in cybersecurity (SOC, IR, red team, GRC, security engineering or similar), AppSec or product security, cloud security, or software engineering.

  • Not a marketer. This role isn't for content or marketing people. If your LinkedIn headline includes the word "storyteller", we respect you, and this isn't the role. Marketers haven't lived the life (neither has the person writing this JD), and the jokes only work if they're real.

  • Funny on the page and on camera, not "has a good personality" funny.

  • Tight writing. You know what works and what to cut. Your grammar can be sub-par; that's the easiest thing to fix.

  • Never punches down. We laugh with the burnt-out CISO, not at them. Vendors are fair game, and that includes Maze: we run the Exploit and we make fun of ourselves too.

  • Reliable. You ship 5 articles and 5 videos a month without anyone chasing you, and you cut the weak ones yourself.

  • Comfortable being named publicly. Your byline goes on every article, and your name, image, voice and likeness appear in the videos we publish and promote, including paid ads. Anonymous accounts and pen names won't work for this role. We know some employers have concerns about this, so you can do the work after hours.

  • Nice to Haves

    • You can shoot and edit your own short-form video

    • You've written sketch, standup, satire, or a security newsletter people actually read

    • You already post on X, Instagram, TikTok, YouTube or LinkedIn

How to Apply

  • 10 headlines. Your own, about security, AI or software, as they'd appear on the Exploit. We read all 10.

  • Video examples. Two or three short videos you've made, on any topic. If you haven't made videos before, record yourself telling one of the stories above in 30 seconds.

  • One sentence on your background. Your role, where you did it, and the worst thing you've seen in production.

Why Join Us

  • Get paid to roast your industry, its vendors and more. The material you've been collecting at work finally has somewhere to go.

  • Upside when a piece lands. We pay like a creator program, not a newsroom, so your best work earns more.

  • A small team. We're starting with two or three people, not forty, so you get real feedback and a direct line to the team.

  • Keep your day job. The role is remote and flexible, and we'd honestly prefer you keep it, since that's where the material comes from.

Compensation

$600 a month base for 5 articles and 5 videos. Any extra content or videos requested by Maze staff beyond the base are agreed project by project.

When one of your pieces performs organically, we often put ad money behind it. If we do, you earn 3% of the spend on top of your base for as long as the ads run. For example, if we spend $5,000 USD on ads, you make $150 more.

This is a contractor role with Maze, not the Exploit.
